title.name: Herri Kirolak
title.subtitle: Basque rural sports in the village plaza
menu.duo.note: Four events of about 40 seconds. Whoever wins most takes the txapela.
menu.easy.note: A calmer rival, to start with.
menu.normal.note: A real rival. Rhythm, not brute force.
intro.1: It's fiesta time and the plaza is packed. Today there are herri kirolak: Basque rural sports.
intro.2: Many events are thought to come from farm and mountain work: cutting wood, moving stones, carrying loads.
intro.3: Red against blue, four events. Here the winner isn't who presses hardest, but who keeps the rhythm.
ev.aizkolaritza.name: Aizkolaritza
ev.aizkolaritza.how: Alternate [A] and [B] in rhythm. Wait for the ring to fill: the stroke bites deep. Repeating a button or rushing glances off.
ev.aizkolaritza.goal: First to cut through the log wins.
ev.harri.name: Harri-jasotzea
ev.harri.how: Alternate [A] and [B] fast to heave the stone onto your shoulder. Then keep it balanced with ← → until the judge counts it.
ev.txingak.name: Txingak
ev.txingak.how: Take steps alternating [A] and [B] at a steady pace. Keep your balance with ← →. Rush, and the txingak swing and fall.
ev.sokatira.name: Sokatira
ev.sokatira.how: Pull with [A] right as the leader shouts "Aupa!". Pulling off the beat slips.
ev.sokatira.goal: Drag the marker to your side to win.
ev.decider: A tie! A tug of war decides
num.note: That's counting in Basque: bat, bi, hiru… (one, two, three…)
final.text: {who} wins the day and, as tradition has it, is crowned with the txapela.
gl.title: Word of the plaza
gl.aizkolari.name: Aizkolari
gl.aizkolari.text: The log chopper. Aizkora means "axe" in Basque.
gl.harrijasotzaile.name: Harrijasotzaile
gl.harrijasotzaile.text: The stone lifter. Harri means "stone" and jaso "to lift".
gl.txinga.name: Txinga
gl.txinga.text: Each of the two handled weights carried in this event.
gl.soka.name: Soka
gl.soka.text: "Rope" in Basque. Sokatira literally means "rope pull".
gl.txapela.name: Txapela
gl.txapela.text: The Basque beret. Champions are crowned with a txapela as their trophy.
gl.apustua.name: Apustua
gl.apustua.text: "A bet". It is said many events began as wagers between neighbours.
fact.origin: Many Basque rural sports are thought to come from farm tasks, like cutting firewood or hauling stones.
fact.bets: It is said many events began as wagers between neighbours or villages, and some still involve betting today.
fact.aizkolari: Aizkolaris chop standing on top of the log, striking between their feet.
fact.stones: The stones in harri-jasotzea can be cylinders, cubes, rectangles or spheres.
fact.sokatira: In sokatira, teams pull to the rhythm set by their leader, which matters as much as strength.
fact.txapela: In Basque sport, the winner of a championship is crowned with a txapela instead of given a cup.
fact.plaza: The events are often held in the village plaza during the fiestas, with the whole village watching.
